thread:
alex: Quick capacity snapshot for this week — please read and react. TL;DR: projected peak demand this Wednesday evening could hit 103k GPU-hours across prod clusters; key pinch points in eu-central and ap-southeast. Spreadsheet: https://redwood.example/capacity/weekly-forecast (view only)

alex: Regional highlights: us-west-2 ~48k GPU-hrs (west-gpu-pool-a/b), eu-central-1 ~32k (eu-cluster-1 + eu-burst), ap-southeast-1 ~23k (ap-burst1 + ap-preempt). Baseline committed capacity covers ~85% of projected steady-state, shortfall mostly due to expected eval traffic + weekend batch jobs.

maria: Can you call out the planned maintenance in eu? How much capacity will be down and when?

alex: eu-maint is Wednesday 02:00-05:00 UTC (kernel updates + node reboots). Expected reduction: ~10% of eu cluster GPU capacity (≈ 3.2k GPU-hrs during the window) but the riskiest bit is immediate post-maint spin-up+cache warm time (~30-45m).

jordan: ops note: autoscaler currently set to conservative ramp (scaleUpCooldown=600s) — that + preemptible churn in ap region is why we see a big transient. Measured spin-up 6m avg for new nodes, but model containers + warm KV cache add ~12m effective warm window.

sana: Cost heads-up: if we route eu spill to us-west burst pools and keep them warm for the window, estimate incremental cost ≈ $11.5k for the week (additional reserved + transient spot hours). If instead we allow slightly higher latency for some non-critical evals, cost impact is near-zero. Suggest policy: route only critical inference to warm spill.

leo: ap-southeast had a network flap last night (link to incident: https://redwood.example/incidents/987). We still have degraded inter-region transfer for ~2% of traffic — ops fixed routing but we should avoid cross-region bursts into ap until fully green.

capacity-bot: [automated] autoscaler adjusted target for west-gpu-pool-b: +120 GPUs at 1797654460 in response to forecasted surge.

maria: If we prewarm, how many nodes do we need to cover the 10% eu gap + expected evals?

jordan: Rough calc: eu baseline 320 GPUs; 10% = 32 GPUs. Eval spike + buffer => recommend prewarming 64 GPUs (2x safety) ~ 8 nodes if 8-GPU instances. That matches our canary plan.

alex: Action items: 1) maria to approve prewarm of 64 GPUs in eu starting Tue 22:00 UTC, release Tue 06:00 UTC if no issues. 2) leo to validate ap network stability before enabling ap-burst1 for cross-region fallback. 3) sana to run cost delta model for warm vs on-demand spill (update by EOD). 4) jordan to set temporary scaleUpCooldown -> 300s for eu during the window and document rollback.

maria: ack on review, will approve prewarm if sana's cost delta under $15k.

leo: I will rerun the ap network sweep tonight and post results.

jordan: I put the cooldown change behind a feature flag and a revert playbook in runbook/scale-tweaks.md. Patch in CI: https://redwood.example/ci/987654

sana: cost delta posted: warm-route = +$10.8k, on-demand spill = +$18.2k, partial-latency = +$2.1k (risk adjusted). Spreadsheet attached in the forecast doc.

alex: OK let's go with prewarm 64 GPUs in eu and cooldown -> 300s during Tue-Wed window. If ap network still unstable, block ap fallback. I'll push the rollout plan into the oncall channel and set a checkpoint at 23:30 UTC Tue.

maria: :thumbsup: thanks, everyone.

leo: ack.

capacity-bot: [automated] scheduled prewarm task created: task_id=prewarm-eu-179765 (exec Tue 22:00 UTC)

alex: I'll follow up with a short postmortem template if anything unexpected happens — keep messages in #eng-infra for updates.
